overview: National grasslands are federal lands, mostly in the Great Plains and West, managed by the U.S. Forest Service, where ranchers often graze livestock under grazing agreements. A section of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act sets rules for grazing permits and leases, including terms and renewals, but currently applies only to national forests in 16 western states. This bill expands that section to cover all National Forest System land, which includes national grasslands, so ranchers there would be treated like permit holders on other federal land. It states that it does not change other laws that govern national grasslands. As of July 23, 2026, the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee had approved it and it was waiting for a vote by the full Senate.
for: Supporters say ranchers on national grasslands should have the same stable permit terms and renewal rights as ranchers on neighboring federal land.
against: Critics say applying permit protections more broadly could make it harder for the Forest Service to adjust grazing to protect grassland health and other uses.
